blocks.text: Here are two reference screenshots of a B2B sales "signal inbox". Build a grid demo from them, but make it noticeably sleeker than the screenshots - feel free to rethink the cell layouts and suggest layout or functional improvements.

I studied both screenshots and the renderer APIs. This is a flat table - one row per contact, horizontally scrollable across ten custom columns, no grouping or pivot. Here's the aspect inventory I stitched from both images:

rows: Flat table, ~6 visible rows, horizontally scrollable (10 columns), no freeze
Leading checkbox column + header select-all checkbox
Gradient avatar, name link, title, @ company - a 3-line rich cell
Signal action line (post = link) + keyword subline
1-3 fire emoji as a discrete score
Relative time, active descending sort in header
Category pills - SMB, Warm Leads, Cold Leads
Footer result count, page-size select, windowed pagination

blocks.text: A few things need your call before I build. My best guess is pre-selected in each:

items.question: Which interactions should actually work in the demo?
items.answer: Column sorting, row selection, pagination, Fit toggle + hover

items.question: How far should I push the "way more sleek" redesign vs. staying faithful to the screenshots?
Confirm the demo id and domain for generated data.

blocks.text: Going with all interactions, a bold redesign, and the id signal-inbox. Here's how each aspect maps to a grid mechanism:

rows: Grid(flat) + FlattenedDataViewModel; cell value = whole Row object
One custom cell renderer per column; static widths give horizontal scroll
Custom facet renderer: uppercase label + sort caret, click rebuilds the viewmodel
Checkbox column + header checkbox; a Set of row ids drives a selected-row tint
Numeric heat chip + 3-pip meter - replaces the fire emoji
Own footer: page-size select + windowed pager over 800 rows
Built-in light + dark pair, all accents from a fixed orange so both modes work

blocks.text: Building it now - viewmodel-only with self-contained generated data, and light/dark counterparts that follow the page theme.
The row hover tint is semi-transparent, so when I hover a row the columns scrolling underneath the pinned checkbox column bleed through it. Can we drop the transparency entirely so rows stay opaque?

Good catch - that's a real bug. The hover and selected backgrounds were mixed against transparent, so on the pinned checkbox fixture the scrolling data columns showed through the translucent tint. The fix: mix the tint against the theme's opaque surface colour instead, so every row background is fully opaque in both light and dark.
The Contact button is too wide. Make it icon-only to shrink the column: an envelope for "not contacted", and a checkmark once contacted.

Icon-only is much tighter. I swapped the text for a currentColor-stroked envelope (Contact) that fills to a solid check (Contacted) on click, and shrank the pinned action column from 150px to a 64px gutter around the 32px button.
Delete the Email column and move the Fit column into its place.
Done - removed Email and moved Fit into its slot. Column order is now Contact, Signal, Score, Fit, Imported, List, Pipeline.

Two cosmetic tweaks: (1) restyle the List column as a small solid colour chip next to a neutral label - like [x] Warm Leads - and mute the colours, there are too many. (2) The Fit control's active colours are too bright; mellow them.

Both in. List is now a 9px solid colour chip plus a neutral-gray label, so the colour is confined to the chip and the column reads calmly instead of a wall of pills. Fit's active fills are mellowed by mixing each verdict colour 80/20 toward slate, keeping the white glyphs legible.
Show a loading spinner while data loads and while paginating, and add a 1s delay to each data load so the loader is actually visible.

Added it. Each sort, page, and page-size change now runs as a simulated async fetch: a frosted overlay with a spinner shows for 1s, then the new page swaps in via updateData(). A load token guards against rapid pager clicks so only the latest load applies.
